newsitem.title: UK: Major faces key parliament vote on EU fish policy.
newsitem.headline: Major faces key parliament vote on EU fish policy.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major may face fresh humiliation over Britain's relations with the European Union on Monday when parliament discusses fishing policy.

Last year's debate on how Britain should fight for EU quotas for its fishermen led to an embarrassing two-vote defeat for Major when Eurosceptic rebels in his Conservative Party refused to endorse his negotiating posture.
Two Conservative legislators voted with the opposition parties and several others abstained in the vote, which the government lost by 301 to 299.
On Thursday, Tony Newton, the cabinet minister in charge of parliamentary business, announced a similar debate for next Monday, just after Major returns from EU talks in Dublin.

With the Eurosceptics a still more potent force in the Conservative Party than a year ago, and with Major now having effectively lost his Commons majority, there is an obvious risk of a further parliamentary defeat.

Such a defeat would not be a threat to the government, but would add to the image of a weak administration struggling to delay a general election until May, the last possible month that it can be held.
This impression is imperilling Major's attempt to claw back the political initiative from the opposition Labour Party, which is expecting a return to the power it has not held since 1979.
Labour was 21 points ahead of the Conservatives in an opinion poll published in Thursday's edition of the Times.
